# LinearModel625

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/BenRD-UM/LinearModel625/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/BenRD-UM/LinearModel625/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/BenRD-UM/LinearModel625/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/BenRD-UM/LinearModel625)
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of LinearModel625 is to replicate the basic working of the base linear
model function in R, stats::lm(). I wanted to learn about QR decomposition and try
and implement it with R C++ integration. I had heard about the Eigen library for
C++ while looking at other packages and wanted to see if I could use it for this
homework.

## Installation

You can install the development version of LinearModel625 like so:

``` r
remotes::install_github("BenRD-UM/LinearModel625")
```

## Example

You can run LinearModel625::lm() exactly the same way as stats::lm() for basic
use cases

```{r example}
library(LinearModel625)
## basic example code
set.seed(123)
n <- 1000
x1 <- rnorm(n, 3, 1)
x2 <- rnorm(n, 10, 3)
eps <- rnorm(n, 0, 1)
y <- 2 + 0.7 * x1 + 0.35 * x2 + eps
sim_df <- data.frame(y = y, var1 = x1, var2 = x2)

# If we have some data that is generated with a clear relationship how does the
# linear model look

mod_625 <- lm(y~.,sim_df)

coef(mod_625)
```

As we can see it correctly identifies the mean and positive relationship of the
two covariates. Additionally we can see that it gives the same beta estimates to
stats::lm().

```{r}
all.equal(coef(mod_625), coef(stats::lm(y~., data = sim_df)))
coef(stats::lm(y~., data = sim_df))
```

I did not match the lm class directly, so integration with summary() and anova()
is not implemented. See the [benchmark vignette](vignettes/benchmarks.html) for more details.
